title: Campaigns: overview and workspace
summary: Understand the Campaigns workspace, its email/SMS channels, subscribers, and where to build, send and measure marketing messages.

body.text: Campaigns is where you send one-off marketing messages to your customers by **email or SMS** and track how they perform. Everything lives under six tabs on the Campaigns page.
The tabs

rows: Compose and send a new email or SMS blast
List of every campaign with status and delivery/engagement figures
Build and save reusable recipient segments
See who is reachable and manage opt-outs
Reusable email subject + body building blocks
Rollup of sends, average open rate and click rate

body.text: Channels

A campaign is either **email** or **SMS**. Each channel must be configured first: email under **Settings → Email**, SMS under **Settings → Integrations**. If neither is set up, the page shows a warning and you cannot send.
Who receives campaigns

Every campaign draws from your **subscribers** — customers who have not opted out of marketing and have an email or phone number on file. Opted-out customers are always excluded, automatically, on every send.
Anyone signed in can view campaigns and analytics. Building, sending and managing audiences requires the campaigns management permission (managers/admins).

title: Campaigns: build and send a campaign
summary: Step-by-step guide to composing an email or SMS campaign, personalising it, sending a test, and starting the send.

body.text: Use the **New campaign** tab to compose and send. The composer shows a live recipient count and lets you send a test to yourself before the real send.

items: Enter a Campaign name (e.g. "Winter service special").
Choose the Channel — Email or SMS. Only configured channels are selectable.
Pick an Audience: "All subscribers" or one of your saved audiences. The recipient count updates live beneath the selector.
For email: optionally choose a template to pre-fill the subject and body, then edit the Subject and write the Email content in the rich-text editor. For SMS: type your Message.
Personalise with {{first_name}} (or {{name}}) — it is replaced with each recipient's name at send time.
Send a test: enter your own email address or phone number and click Send test to preview the real message.
Click Send campaign, then confirm in the dialog to start the send.

body.text: What happens on send

The campaign is created and the **first batch (60 recipients)** goes out immediately so you get instant progress. The rest are drained automatically in the background by a scheduled queue. The campaign status moves **queued → sending → sent** as batches complete, and progress appears on the Campaigns list and the campaign's own page.
For email, the unsubscribe link and open/click tracking are added automatically — you do not add them yourself. Your content is also wrapped in the Denago Cape Town branded email shell.
If no opted-in contacts match the chosen audience, the send is rejected. Preview the recipient count first.

title: Campaigns: audiences and subscribers
summary: Build reusable recipient segments from source, tag, province and customer traits, and manage who is opted in or out.

body.text: Audiences are saved recipient filters you can reuse across campaigns. Build them on the **Audiences** tab; manage opt-ins on the **Subscribers** tab.
Build an audience

items: On the Audiences tab, use the New audience card to set any combination of filters: Source (manual, facebook, instagram, website, whatsapp), Tag, and Province.
Optionally tick trait filters: Owns a cart, Service due, or Bought before (a won deal).
Click Preview count to see how many subscribers match.
Give it a name and click Save audience — it appears under Saved audiences and becomes selectable in the composer.

body.text: Saved audiences list their matching recipient count and can be deleted. All audience filters automatically exclude opted-out contacts, and the **Service due** filter only keeps carts whose service status is due-soon or overdue.
Subscribers and opt-outs

The Subscribers tab counts who is **Subscribed** (not opted out, with an email or phone) versus **Unsubscribed**. Use the **Unsubscribe** button beside a customer to opt them out, and **Resubscribe** in the collapsible list to opt them back in.
An audience reaches at most 5,000 contacts per send. SMS audiences require a WhatsApp/phone number; email audiences require an email address.

title: Campaigns: tracking, opens, clicks and analytics
summary: How opens, clicks and unsubscribes are tracked, how to read per-campaign results, and why open rates are only approximate.

body.text: Email campaigns are tracked automatically. The **Analytics** tab gives an account-wide rollup, and each campaign has its own results page.
Account rollup

The Analytics tab shows total campaigns, messages sent, **average open rate**, **average click rate**, subscribers and unsubscribed counts, plus a table of recent email campaigns with per-campaign open and click percentages.
Per-campaign detail

Open any campaign to see recipients, sent/failed counts, opened and clicked percentages, and a per-recipient table with each person's status and open/click counts. Failed recipients show the error reason. Email campaigns also offer a **Preview email** panel.
How tracking works

items: Opens: an invisible 1×1 tracking pixel loads when the email is viewed.
Clicks: links in the email are rewritten so clicks are counted before the recipient reaches the destination.
Unsubscribes: the auto-added footer link opts the customer out of future marketing.

body.text: Open rates are approximate — some mail apps (e.g. Apple Mail Privacy Protection) auto-load the pixel and image-blocking hides it. Treat clicks as the reliable engagement signal. SMS campaigns do not report opens or clicks.

title: Surveys: overview and survey types
summary: Understand CSAT, sales, NPS and ad-hoc surveys, the metrics they produce, and how feedback rolls up across all surveys.

body.text: The **Surveys & feedback** module collects customer ratings and comments. It tracks CSAT, NPS and post-sale feedback, and rolls the results up into headline metrics.
Survey types

rows: Auto-sends when a job card is completed

body.text: Headline metrics

items: Responses — completed responses across all surveys.
Response rate — completed ÷ sent (failed sends excluded).
Avg CSAT — average star rating out of 5 across service and sales surveys.
NPS — % promoters (score 9–10) minus % detractors (0–6), from −100 to +100.

body.text: Create a survey

items: In the New survey card, enter a title (e.g. "Post-service satisfaction").
Choose a type — sensible questions and a default trigger are pre-filled.
Click Create; you land in the survey editor to refine everything.

body.text: Surveys can be viewed by CRM staff; creating, editing and sending require the surveys management permission. Deleting a survey soft-deletes it (it is recoverable, not purged).

title: Surveys: build questions and set the trigger
summary: Use the survey builder to write questions, set intro and thank-you text, and control when and how quickly a survey sends.

body.text: Open a survey to reach the builder. Changes are held until you click **Save survey**; the status indicator shows Unsaved changes / Saving / Saved.
Basics and sending rules

items: Set the Survey name.
Choose When should it send: Manual only, or automatically when a job card is completed, a cart is delivered, or a deal is won.
Tick Active so it is allowed to send (unticking pauses all sends).
For triggered surveys, set a Send delay in hours or days — 0 means it sends immediately when the event happens.
Write the Intro message (shown on the form and in the invite) and the Thank-you message (shown after submitting).

body.text: Add and edit questions
Add questions of four kinds and reorder them with the up/down arrows:

items: Star rating — choose a 1–5 or 1–10 scale.
NPS (0–10) — set the low and high end labels.
Multiple choice — one option per line, optionally allowing multiple selections.
Comment / text — optionally multi-line.

body.text: Rating, NPS and choice questions can be marked **Required**. Use the type selector plus **+ Add question** to add more, and **Remove** to delete one.
A survey's headline stat adapts to its type: NPS surveys show an NPS score; rating-based surveys show an average out of 5.

title: Surveys: send to an audience and read responses
summary: Send a survey manually to a chosen segment or via automatic triggers, and review scores, comments and completion status.

body.text: A survey reaches customers two ways: **automatically** at a natural moment (if it has a trigger) or **manually** to an audience you pick from the survey's Send panel.
Send manually

items: In the Send this survey panel, choose an audience: Send a test to myself, All customers (reachable, not opted out), Cart owners (have a vehicle on file), or Customers who bought (won deals).
Click Send now.
The result reports how many were sent and how many were skipped.

body.text: Recipients receive only one survey of each type every 30 days, so resending is safe. Skips happen when a customer was recently surveyed, has opted out, or has no contact detail.
Automatic sending

If the survey has a trigger, it also fires on its own: CSAT surveys send when a **job card is completed**, sales surveys when a **cart is delivered** or a **deal is won** — after any configured delay. The editor shows a note describing the exact automatic behaviour and wait time.
Reading responses

The Responses table lists each recipient, their score, their comment, a status of **completed** or **pending**, and when. Customers are linked to their contact record. Failed sends are hidden from the counts, and the summary shows the completion rate and the type-appropriate score (average rating or NPS).

title: Automations: lead workflow rules
summary: Create when-then rules that react to lead events — schedule activities, send emails, move stages, assign owners or notify the team.

body.text: Automations are simple **when-this-happens, do-that** rules for your sales pipeline. Each rule pairs one trigger with one action, and every firing is recorded in a run log.
Create a rule

items: Click New automation and give the rule a clear name.
Choose the When trigger (see table). Some triggers need a detail: a stage for "enters a stage", or a number of days for "sits untouched".
Optionally open "Only if…" to restrict the rule: lead source is one of a comma-separated list, and/or lead value at least a rand amount.
Choose the Then action and fill its fields.
Save. The rule fires automatically from then on.

rows: Schedule an activity (call, email, meeting, WhatsApp, test drive or to-do) due in N days
Send an email template to the lead
A lead sits untouched N days
Move the lead to a stage
Assign the lead to a team member
A quote is signed / declined online
Send the team a push notification
A cart is delivered, or a referral fee is earned

body.text: Activities can be assigned to a specific team member or default to the lead owner. Push messages support the placeholders **{{name}}**, **{{model}}** and **{{value}}**.
Manage rules

items: Pause / Resume — temporarily stop a rule without deleting it (paused rules are dimmed).
Edit rule — expand a rule inline to change it.
Delete — removes the rule and its run history; this cannot be undone.
Recent runs — a live log showing which rule fired for which lead, with a ✓ or ✕ for success or failure.

body.text: Sending an email action needs at least one email template (Settings → Email templates). Creating and editing automations is restricted to owners/admins.

title: Journeys: multi-step marketing automations
summary: Understand versioned, multi-step journeys, how they differ from simple rules, and how to install recommended starter drafts.

body.text: Journeys are **versioned, multi-step workflows** — the advanced sibling of Automations, reached via **Automations → Journeys**. Where an automation rule does one thing, a journey chains waits, messages, CRM actions and conditional branches, and enrols leads or contacts over time.
Key concepts

items: Category — each journey is a CRM automation or a Marketing journey.
Versions — edits create a new draft; publishing makes that version active and retires the previous one.
Status — draft, active, paused or archived. A journey must be published before it can be activated.
Runs — each enrolled lead or contact becomes a run you can track, retry or cancel.

body.text: Start from recommended drafts
Click **Install recommended drafts** to add four ready-made journeys as drafts you can review, edit and publish:

rows: Instantly notifies the team and creates a same-day follow-up task
Sends a welcome email a day after a lead is won
Annual anniversary greeting for vehicle owners
Re-engages owners inactive for 12 months, then follows up

body.text: If the legacy anniversary or win-back toggles are still on in Settings, a banner warns you to disable them before activating equivalent journeys — otherwise customers could receive both versions.
Journeys are owner/admin-only, from viewing through publishing.

title: Journeys: build, publish and monitor runs
summary: Configure a journey's enrollment trigger, entry filters and ordered steps, publish a version, enroll records, and manage runs.

body.text: The journey builder has three parts: an enrollment trigger, optional entry filters, and an ordered list of steps. Save your work as a **draft**, then publish it to go live.
1. Enrollment trigger

Choose what enrolls a record: new lead created, lead enters a stage, lead becomes idle, lead won/lost, quote signed/declined, vehicle delivered, referral earned, **contact joins a saved segment**, **purchase anniversary**, or **inactive customer win-back**. Some triggers take config — a stage, idle days, a segment plus re-enrollment frequency (once / weekly / daily), or the number of inactive months.
2. Optional entry filters
Narrow enrollment by **lead source** (comma-separated), **province**, and/or a **minimum lead value** in rands. All specified filters must match.
3. Journey steps
Add steps and order them with the up/down arrows. Available step types:

items: Send email — pick a template or write a subject and body.
Send SMS / Notify the team — a message.
Wait — a number of minutes, hours or days before the next step.
Create activity — type, summary, due days, and owner.
Move lead stage, Assign lead, Add contact tag, Remove contact tag.
Condition / branch — matching records continue; non-matches stop safely.
Stop journey.

body.text: Messages support the placeholders **{{first_name}}**, **{{name}}**, **{{model}}** and **{{value}}**. A journey can hold up to 50 steps and 30 conditions.
Publish and run

items: Save draft to store your changes as a new draft version.
Click Publish v{n} to make that version active — the journey status becomes active.
Use Pause / Resume to control an active journey.
For idle-lead, segment, anniversary and win-back journeys, click Enroll now to enroll matching records immediately.
Use Archive to retire a journey.

body.text: Monitor runs

The **Recent journey runs** table shows each run's journey, record (lead/contact), version, status, current step, start time and any error. **Retry** failed or cancelled runs; **Cancel** runs that are still queued or waiting.
Editing a published journey creates a fresh draft — the live version keeps running until you publish the new one, so you can revise safely.
